description: DiligenceOps: submit subprocessor claims, as a statement, a list or entries with name, purpose and location, and the agreement or subprocessor list offered for them. The signed report pairs the processors by name (legal suffixes set aside, AWS and Amazon Web Services as one) and lists those missing from the evidence, those the evidence adds and those whose purpose or location changed, with quotes. POST /api/subprocessor-evidence-check. Reads only the material in the call: no page fetch, no account access, no merchant contact and no money movement. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. The report matches words, figures, dates and named items between the submitted texts; it does not interpret meaning beyond that matching. Contract: /api/diligence-vendor-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/diligence-checks/.

name.description: The subprocessor as named, for example "Amazon Web Services, Inc.".

claims.description: The subprocessors as claimed: a statement or list as text, or up to 200 entries as names or {name, purpose, location}.

claims_label.description: Optional name for the material, recorded in the report.

evidence.description: The data processing agreement, subprocessor list or other evidence. As text, or up to 200 excerpts as {source, text}. Up to 256 KB in all.

evidence_label.description: Optional name for the material, recorded in the report.

format.description: html reduces the markup to readable text first. Defaults to html when the text starts with a tag, otherwise text.
